chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī, from al-Faḍl ibn Muḥammad, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Zakariyyā, from al-Walīd ibn Abān, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام led us in the ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers when the sun had declined, with one adhān and two iqāmahs. Then he said: “I have a need to attend to, so perform supererogatory prayers.”

key_terms.إِقَامَتَيْنِ: two iqāmahs; one commencement call for each salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَاجَةٍ: a need or matter requiring attention
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined; referring to the sun passing the meridian

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about praying ẓuhr and ʿaṣr together with one adhān and two iqāmahs?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام performed the ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers at the time of the sun’s decline, using one adhān and two iqāmahs. It indicates a practical precedent related to the timing and performance of the daily salat and the offering of supererogatory prayer afterward.
